technology_name: A METHOD FOR SUPPRESSING LEIDENFROST EFFECT AND INCREASING HEAT TRANSFER RATE IN IMMERSION COOLING USING ELECTROPHORESIS
institution: National Institute of Technology Calicut (NIT Calicut)
problem_solved: High-temperature industrial immersion cooling triggers the Leidenfrost effect, creating an insulating vapor blanket around hot elements that stalls heat dissipation and triggers thermal runaways.
description: An electro-hydrodynamic cooling control methodology that applies high-frequency DC electric potentials into an Al2O3 nanoparticle-infused TiO2 ionic liquid host to suppress vapor blankets via automated electrophoretic fluid agitation.
applications: Nuclear reactor core safety loops, high-power server immersion cooling networks, metal foundry quenching systems, and high-load EV battery thermal cells.
contact_person: INVADLIA DR. SUJITH KUMAR C S
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, Digital Technologies, AI & Software, Infrastructure, Construction & Smart Cities
